why: A protected path is protected by its name. A rename gives the same bytes a second name that no entry covers, and a DELETE leaves the same artefact: content that was protected, reachable through `git show <sha>^:<path>`, under a name the guard reads as ordinary documentation. This ledger is the tracked copy, so the guard works in a shallow clone, in a `git archive` export, and with no git binary at all -- the derivation from `git log --diff-filter=RD` only cross-checks it.
